_about: Press conference questions (Stage 6.3, src/sim/career/press.ts). Each question has a phase (pre: before the next match, post: after this week's), the tag that brings it, and three answers: calm, bold and deflect. 'label' is what the owner says (the paper quotes it), 'reply' is how the room takes it. Effects: fans, squad (every player's mood), mood (the player the question is about), press, heat (rivalry with the opponent), claim (a promise to win the next match, judged after it). Fills: {us} {them} {city} {nick} {coach} {player} {first} {score} {stage} {cup} {n} {pos}. Every name here is made up.

questions.text: It's {them} this week. What does a derby mean to you?

calm.label: It matters to the fans, so it matters to us. We'll prepare like any other match.
calm.reply: Sensible. Nobody will pin that one on a dressing-room wall.

bold.label: This is our city. We'll remind {them} of that on Saturday.
bold.reply: The pens move very fast. {them} will have read it by lunch.

deflect.label: Ask me after the match.
deflect.reply: A few groans. Not much of a headline in that.

questions.text: The {them} fans have been singing about you. Any message for them?

calm.label: I hope they enjoy the game. Ours will be louder.
calm.reply: A smile or two. It reads well.

bold.label: They can sing. Their team can't play.
bold.reply: Your fans will love it. Theirs will print it on a banner.

deflect.label: I didn't hear it. Must have been a quiet day.
deflect.reply: Laughter round the room. Even the grumpy ones wrote it down.

questions.text: Derby pressure is a different thing. Will your players cope?

calm.label: They've played big games before. They'll be fine.
calm.reply: The players will like that you backed them.

bold.label: The pressure is on {them}. They're the ones who should be worried.
bold.reply: Bold. It had better come off.

deflect.label: No pressure from me. I just pay the wages.
deflect.reply: It got a laugh, and the dressing room won't mind it.

questions.text: {us} against {them}, both near the top. Is this a title decider?

calm.label: It's three points. Big ones, but there's a long way to go.
calm.reply: Measured. The press like a measured owner.

bold.label: We're going to win this league, and this is where we show it.
bold.reply: That's tomorrow's back page, and it will follow you all week.

deflect.label: Ask me at the end of the season.
deflect.reply: Fair enough, but it won't sell papers.

questions.text: The bookmakers make {them} favourites this week. Fair?

calm.label: They've earned that. We'll try to change a few minds.
calm.reply: Respectful, and it takes some pressure off the players.

bold.label: The bookmakers are about to lose a lot of money.
bold.reply: The room loves it. Someone asks if you've placed a bet.

deflect.label: I don't gamble. I bought a football club, so I've done enough of that.
deflect.reply: Big laugh. That one will be quoted for a while.

questions.text: The {stage} against {them}. Is the squad ready?

calm.label: They've worked all season for this. We're ready.
calm.reply: Calm words before a big night. The players will take it in.

bold.label: We didn't come this far to go out to {them}.
bold.reply: Fighting talk. The whole of {city} will hold you to it.

deflect.label: We'll find out on the night.
deflect.reply: Honest, if not exciting.

questions.text: How much is a run in the {cup} worth to the club?

calm.label: The money helps, but the players are thinking about football, and so am I.
calm.reply: The right answer, and they know it.

bold.label: A lot. And we intend to collect every cent of it.
bold.reply: Some of the room winces. The fans don't mind.

deflect.label: Ask the accountants. They've been smiling all week.
deflect.reply: A laugh, and nothing to use against you.

questions.text: One match from the {cup}. What will you tell the players?

calm.label: Enjoy it. Days like this don't come often.
calm.reply: Warm words. The players will walk out a little lighter.

bold.label: {city} wants a parade, and we're going to give it one.
bold.reply: The city goes wild. If it goes wrong, it will be on every front page.

deflect.label: That's between me and them.
deflect.reply: Fair. The players appreciate it.

questions.text: There's been bad blood with {them} after what's been said. Will you calm things down?

calm.label: Things were said in the heat of it. I respect {them}.
calm.reply: A peace offering. The press approve, some fans less so.

bold.label: I meant every word.
bold.reply: Here we go again. The paper will make a week of it.

deflect.label: I'll let the football do the talking.
deflect.reply: Neither peace nor war. The room moves on.

questions.text: Any team news ahead of {them}?

calm.label: The coach picks the team. My job is to make sure there are good players to pick from.
calm.reply: Proper, and it keeps the head coach on side.

bold.label: Whoever plays, it will be too much for {them}.
bold.reply: Confident. The players will read it, and so will {them}.

deflect.label: Nice try.
deflect.reply: A few laughs. Nobody expected an answer.

questions.text: Do you want a big crowd behind the team for {them}?

calm.label: Always. The fans make the difference in games like this.
calm.reply: The supporters' groups will share that one.

bold.label: If you haven't got a ticket, you're going to regret it.
bold.reply: A promise of a show. It had better be one.

deflect.label: Ask the box office.
deflect.reply: A shrug from the room.

questions.text: {us} are {pos} in the table. Happy with that?

calm.label: Happy with the work. There's more to come.
calm.reply: Nothing to argue with.

bold.label: We should be higher, and we will be.
bold.reply: The players hear ambition. Some of them hear pressure.

deflect.label: I don't look at the table until the end.
deflect.reply: Nobody believes you, but it's a tidy answer.

questions.text: {score} against {them}. The best performance of the season?

calm.label: A very good day. We'll enjoy it tonight and get back to work tomorrow.
calm.reply: Grounded. The press like that after a big win.

bold.label: The best in years. Anyone who wants to stop us will have to play a lot better than {them}.
bold.reply: The fans will love it. {them} won't forget it.

deflect.label: Ask the players. They did the work.
deflect.reply: The dressing room will hear that you gave them the credit.

questions.subject: hero
questions.text: {player} was outstanding. Is he the best in the league right now?

calm.label: He's in great form. Long may it last.
calm.reply: Praise without pressure. {first} will take it.

bold.label: The best in the league, and he's not for sale. Not at any price.
bold.reply: {first} is delighted. Agents everywhere just wrote his name down.

deflect.label: One game. Let's not get carried away.
deflect.reply: Fair, but {first} might have liked a kinder word.

questions.text: {score}. How do you explain that?

calm.label: We weren't good enough and I won't pretend otherwise. We'll put it right.
calm.reply: Honest. The press respect it.

bold.label: Unacceptable. If it happens again, some of them won't be wearing this shirt for long.
bold.reply: The fans cheer it. The dressing room goes very quiet.

deflect.label: I'm not going to talk about individuals tonight.
deflect.reply: The room wanted more. They'll write their own version.

questions.text: Is {coach}'s job safe?

calm.label: {coach} has my full support. One bad day doesn't change that.
calm.reply: A vote of confidence. The players notice.

bold.label: Everyone at this club is judged on results. Everyone.
bold.reply: That will be read in the coach's office. And the dressing room.

deflect.label: I'm not having that conversation in public.
deflect.reply: Which the paper will take as a no.

questions.text: Nobody gave {us} a chance against {them}. Did you?

calm.label: I always believe in this team. Today they showed why.
calm.reply: The players will like that.

bold.label: I did. I'm not sure why anyone else didn't.
bold.reply: A little smug, and the fans don't care.

deflect.label: I had a feeling. Mostly in my stomach, but still.
deflect.reply: Laughter. A good day all round.

questions.text: Losing to {them}, of all teams. Embarrassing?

calm.label: Disappointing. Credit to {them}, they wanted it more.
calm.reply: Gracious. The press note it.

bold.label: Embarrassing is the word. The players know it, and they'll hear it from me.
bold.reply: The fans agree. The players won't enjoy Monday.

deflect.label: Any team in this league can beat anyone.
deflect.reply: True enough. Not much else to write.

questions.text: That's {n} defeats in a row. Is this a crisis?

calm.label: It's a bad run. Bad runs end. We stick together.
calm.reply: Steady. The dressing room needed to hear it.

bold.label: If the players don't turn it around, I'll find players who will.
bold.reply: The fans like the anger. The players don't like the threat.

deflect.label: I don't use that word.
deflect.reply: The paper will use it for you.

questions.text: The fans are angry. What do you say to them?

calm.label: They're right to be. They pay their money and they deserve better. We'll give it to them.
calm.reply: It lands well in the stands.

bold.label: Stick with us. This team will come good, and you'll want to say you were there.
bold.reply: A promise. The fans will remember it, one way or another.

deflect.label: I hear them. I'm not making promises tonight.
deflect.reply: Cold comfort for the people in the stands.

questions.text: {n} wins in a row. How far can this team go?

calm.label: One game at a time. It's a cliché because it's true.
calm.reply: Safe, and nobody can say it's wrong.

bold.label: All the way. Why not us?
bold.reply: The fans start dreaming. So does the paper.

deflect.label: I'm wearing the same socks until we lose. Don't ask me anything else.
deflect.reply: The room loves it. Expect a photo request.

questions.text: Out of the {cup}. Was the season a failure?

calm.label: No. We made the playoffs and we'll learn from tonight.
calm.reply: Fair. The players will be grateful for it.

bold.label: Going out is never good enough. There will be changes in the off-season.
bold.reply: The dressing room has a long off-season to think about that.

deflect.label: Ask me when the dust settles.
deflect.reply: Understandable on a night like this.

questions.text: {us} have won the {cup}! What does it mean?

calm.label: Everything. To the players, the staff and every fan who stuck with us.
calm.reply: Applause in the press room. That doesn't happen often.

bold.label: It means this is just the start.
bold.reply: The city loves it. Every rival just circled next season.

deflect.label: Give me a minute. I'm still soaked.
deflect.reply: Someone hands you a towel. Big laugh.

questions.text: Bragging rights to {us}. A message for the {them} fans?

calm.label: Hard luck. See you next time.
calm.reply: Gracious in victory. The press approve.

bold.label: Get used to it.
bold.reply: Three words, a lot of noise. {them} fans won't let it go.

deflect.label: I'll let our fans do the talking tonight.
deflect.reply: They will. Loudly.

questions.text: Losing the derby. How does that feel?

calm.label: It hurts. It's meant to. We'll be ready for the next one.
calm.reply: Honest, and the fans feel the same.

bold.label: They can enjoy it while it lasts. We won't forget it.
bold.reply: A grudge, on the record. The next derby just got bigger.

deflect.label: I'm not talking about them tonight.
deflect.reply: Which says plenty.

questions.subject: hatTrick
questions.text: A hat-trick for {player}. Where does he rank?

calm.label: He's having a fine season. Credit to the coaches too.
calm.reply: Praise shared around. Nobody minds.

bold.label: He's the best striker in Valmere. Write that down.
bold.reply: {first} is walking on air. Every agent in the country just took note.

deflect.label: He'll be the first to say the team made it easy.
deflect.reply: The team-mates like hearing it.

questions.subject: redCard
questions.text: {player} was sent off. Did he let the team down?

calm.label: He knows he got it wrong. He'll learn from it.
calm.reply: Backing your player. {first} will be grateful.

bold.label: Yes. He'll be fined, and he knows why.
bold.reply: Strong, and public. {first} won't enjoy reading it.

deflect.label: I haven't seen it again yet.
deflect.reply: Everyone has seen it again. The room smiles.

questions.text: Were you happy with the referee against {them}?

calm.label: Referees have a hard job. We move on.
calm.reply: The league office will be pleased with you.

bold.label: No. And I'll be writing to the league about it.
bold.reply: The fans cheer. The league won't.

deflect.label: I'd like to keep my money, thanks.
deflect.reply: Laughter. Everyone knows what you mean.

questions.text: Will you put more money into the team?

calm.label: We'll spend when it's right for the club, not to win a headline.
calm.reply: Sensible. Some fans wanted more.

bold.label: Whatever it takes. I didn't buy this club to finish mid-table.
bold.reply: The fans love it. Every agent in Valmere just raised their prices.

deflect.label: My accountant reads your paper, so no comment.
deflect.reply: A laugh, and no promise to hold you to.

questions.text: Will we see more of the academy players?

calm.label: When they're ready. The best ones won't be held back.
calm.reply: Hard to argue with.

bold.label: Yes. This club should be built on {city} kids.
bold.reply: The fans love it. A few senior players shift in their seats.

deflect.label: That's for the coaches.
deflect.reply: Fair. Not much of a story.

questions.text: How is the mood in the dressing room after {them}?

calm.label: Good. They're a close group and they work hard for each other.
calm.reply: The players will read that and nod.

bold.label: Hungry. Nobody here is satisfied yet.
bold.reply: The fans like hungry.

deflect.label: You'd have to ask them. I just knock before I go in.
deflect.reply: A laugh. The players will like that one too.

questions.text: Is {coach} still the right head coach for {us}?

calm.label: Yes. We judge over a season, not a week.
calm.reply: A clear vote of confidence. The coach will be glad of it.

bold.label: Everyone here is judged on results. Me included.
bold.reply: Honest, and a little chilly. The dressing room noticed.

deflect.label: I'm not doing that question.
deflect.reply: Which the room takes as an answer of sorts.

questions.text: What did you learn about this team against {them}?

calm.label: That they keep going. That's what I want to see.
calm.reply: Simple and fair.

bold.label: That there's a lot more in them, and I want all of it.
bold.reply: Ambitious. The players feel the bar going up.

deflect.label: That the coffee in this room is still terrible.
deflect.reply: The best laugh of the afternoon.

questions.text: What does this club mean to {city} right now?

calm.label: Everything. We try to remember that every day.
calm.reply: Warm words. The local radio played them twice.

bold.label: It should mean more, and we're going to make sure it does.
bold.reply: Big talk, and the city likes big talk.

deflect.label: You'd have to ask {city}.
deflect.reply: A little flat for a question like that.

questions.text: How have you prepared for {them}?

calm.label: Same as every week. Work hard, respect the opponent.
calm.reply: Nothing to see here, which is the point.

bold.label: We know exactly how to beat {them}. Watch.
bold.reply: That is going on the {them} dressing room wall.

deflect.label: I watched a lot of video. Mostly of my dog.
deflect.reply: Laughter. No one learned a thing.

questions.text: What do you make of {them}?

calm.label: Good side, well coached. We'll have to be at our best.
calm.reply: Respectful. Their coach will appreciate it.

bold.label: They're fine. We're better.
bold.reply: Short, and it will be quoted all week.

deflect.label: I try not to think about other teams too much.
deflect.reply: A non-answer, politely given.

questions.text: Is there pressure on the team this week?

calm.label: There's always pressure at a club like this. It's a good thing.
calm.reply: Measured. The players stay calm too.

bold.label: The pressure is on {them}, not us.
bold.reply: A jab, and it lands.

deflect.label: Only on the person who books the team bus.
deflect.reply: A laugh, and the subject changes.

bold: "{quote}"|The {us} owner did not hold back at the press conference {context}.
{us} owner talks big {context}|"{quote}" Bold words. The whole league heard them.
Owner's fighting talk {context}|"{quote}" There's no taking that back now.

Calm words from the {us} owner {context}|"{quote}" No drama, and that seemed to be the point.
deflect: {us} owner gives little away {context}|Asked the questions everyone wanted asked, the owner offered: "{quote}"
Not much from the {us} owner {context}|"{quote}" The press room wanted more.
staff: {assistant} faces the press for {us}|The owner sent the assistant coach to the press conference {context}. Nothing controversial was said.
